# 2nd Act Franchise Expo — Zoom presentation assets

Standalone, self-contained build for Kelsey Stuart's 15-minute presentation at the 2nd Act
Franchise Expo. **Isolated from the Next.js app** — its own `package.json`, never add these
deps to the root. Lives on git branch `expo/2nd-act-assets` (not merged to `main`).

## Deliverables (`out/`, regenerated by the scripts — gitignored)
| File | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `background.png` | Virtual background (on screen ~2/3 of the session) | Mountain plate + content on cream cards |
| `slide-1-intro.png` | Slide 1 — introduction | |
| `slide-2-method.png` | Slide 2 — method ("Pilates or popcorn?") | Load-bearing, stark |
| `slide-3-questions.png` | Slide 3 — three questions (verbatim) | |
| `slide-4-qr.png` | Slide 4 — QR push | Doc dominant, booking secondary |
| `qr-doc.png` / `qr-doc-bg.png` | Doc QR (slide / background sizes) | Encodes `https://waypointfranchise.com/guide` |
| `qr-booking.png` | Booking QR | Encodes the TidyCal link |
| `calibration-grid.png` | Safe-zone calibration grid | See "Calibration" below |

All five images are **1920×1080 PNG, sRGB (ICC attached), no alpha** — asserted at build.

## Regenerate everything
```bash
cd expo-2nd-act
npm install
npx playwright install chromium   # one-time; downloads to OS cache, not the repo
npm run all                        # QR -> images -> verify-qr -> verify-final
```
`npm run all` regenerates QRs, renders all assets, and runs both QR verification suites.
Individual steps: `npm run qr`, `npm run images`, `npm run verify-qr`, `npm run grid`.

### If a link or the phone number changes
- **Phone / email / site:** edit `CONTACT` in `tokens.mjs`, then `npm run images`.
- **Doc or booking URL:** the Doc QR points at `waypointfranchise.com/guide` (a redirect on
  the live site — see below), so the QR never changes when the Doc moves; just repoint the
  redirect. To change the booking link, edit `URLS.booking` in `tokens.mjs` and `npm run all`.
- **The `/guide` redirect** lives in the repo-root `next.config.ts` (on `main`, deployed to
  production): `waypointfranchise.com/guide` → the Google Doc's **`/copy`** endpoint (307
  temporary). `/copy` makes every visitor get their **own editable copy** of the guide (take
  notes; one copy per brand) instead of a shared read-only view — visitors must be signed
  into a Google account to copy. Change the destination there to repoint the guide without
  touching any asset. (The Doc must stay shared "Anyone with the link — Viewer" to be copyable.)

## Colors (from the live site `src/app/globals.css`, "Rustic Editorial")
Defined in `tokens.mjs`. Every graphic/type color maps to one of these; the mountain plate
is imagery and exempt.
- Cream canvas: `#F5F0E8` / `#FAF8F4` (light) / `#EDE7DA` (dark, used for hairlines)
- Navy: `#0c1929` (primary type/headlines)
- Copper (accent/display only — `#8E3012`, ~6.2:1 on cream; **never** small body text)
- Text: charcoal `#1a1a1a`, stone `#4a4a4a`, muted `#7a7a7a`
- QR: pure `#000` on `#fff` (21:1 contrast)

## Fonts
Vendored (the live-site typefaces), in `fonts/`, declared in `templates/fonts.css`:
- **Inter** (400/500/600/700) — body/UI
- **Playfair Display** (400/500/600/700/800/900 + 400/700 italic) — headlines, accents

Rendering is Playwright (headless Chromium) → the screenshot is gated on
`document.fonts.load()` per weight, so fonts never silently fall back (a font smoke test in
`build-images.mjs` fails the build if they do). `sharp` then flattens to opaque sRGB+ICC.

## Layout (attendee-true coordinates, 1920×1080)
- **Slides**: `slide-base.css` sets 132px side margins, 96px top; a copper rule + a small
  footer wordmark carry cohesion. Smallest text ≥46px (legible when the tile halves to 960×540).
- **Background safe zone** (derived from Kelsey's calibration + confirmed by a live load):
  his body occupies roughly the center **x 460–1460, y 260–1080**. Content is kept clear of it:
  - Wordmark + anchor line: top-left (`x 80, y 60–216`).
  - Contact block (cream card, left-aligned): top-right (`right:70, top:56`).
  - Doc fallback QR (cream card): right band (`left:1460, top:452`, 360px QR).
  All content sits in the top strip + right band, well clear of the presenter.

## Calibration method (how the safe zone was measured)
1. In Logi Options+, disable Brio auto-framing / lock the FOV (so the obscured region is
   stable for the whole session).
2. In Zoom, uncheck **"Mirror my video"** (otherwise the capture is horizontally flipped;
   attendees always see the un-mirrored frame).
3. Load `calibration-grid.png` as the Zoom virtual background; sit in the real presenting
   position; screenshot the full video tile (speaker view, full screen) as a lossless PNG.
4. The grid has four orange corner registration marks + coordinate labels every 120px:
   crop to the marks, rescale to 1920×1080, trace the body silhouette, add an ~8–10% movement
   buffer. The complement is the usable safe zone.
Never pre-flip text/QR — Zoom transmits the background un-mirrored to attendees.

## QR verification (why these codes will scan off a compressed Zoom tile)
- ECC level **H**, ≥4-module quiet zone, square modules, pure black/white, generated locally
  (`qrcode`), no hosted service or third-party shortener.
- Sizes: background 360px, slide-4 doc 540px (dominant), booking 441px (all ≥ the brief minimums).
- `verify-qr.mjs` / `verify-final.mjs` decode every code with **two independent engines**
  (`@undecaf/zbar-wasm` + `@zxing/library`) after a **4:2:0 JPEG re-encode** that simulates
  Zoom's video compression — at 1920×1080, 960×540, and (background) 640×360.
- **Safety margin:** every code still decodes on both engines down to **JPEG quality 30** at
  the smallest test size — well past realistic Zoom compression. The `/guide` short redirect
  keeps the Doc code low-density (version 5) precisely so it survives the compressed background.

## Files
- `tokens.mjs` — colors, contact, URLs, sizes (single source of truth)
- `templates/` — HTML/CSS per asset + shared `fonts.css` / `slide-base.css`
- `build-images.mjs` — Playwright render → sharp normalize → metadata assertion
- `build-qr.mjs` — local QR generation (flattened sRGB+ICC) + self-verification
- `qr-lib.mjs` — QR generation + dual-decoder helpers + compression simulation
- `verify-qr.mjs` / `verify-final.mjs` — decode matrices (in-memory / on the shipped files)
- `copy.md` — approved on-slide copy (source of truth for the text)
- `plate/` — the Higgsfield mountain plate (V1) + 1920×1080 scaled version
- `fonts/` — vendored Inter + Playfair Display
